deviations.from: five misconception register entries with topic_id 6.3, carried as MISCON cards
deviations.to: misconception blocks and misconception_correction claims inside the five planned content units, with the discriminations practised inside the 16 slot items
deviations.why: the 6.3 work order contains no MISCON slots, so the register entries are taught and practised within the 20 planned items rather than as extra cards beyond the planned count, following the recorded precedent of topic 2.3.

deviations.from: the birth rate vs natural increase register entry, filed under OBJ-0455-6.3.1
deviations.why: the entry's content is population measures owned by the population topics of unit 5; teaching them inside a foreign exchange topic would be scope creep, and the confusion is better practised where its content lives.

deviations.from: the interest-rate direction and the low-inflation-level-vs-fall register entries, both filed under OBJ-0455-6.3.1
deviations.to: taught in CU-0455-6.3.3, where their content sits among the causes of fluctuations
deviations.why: the register's objective filing reflects the series in which each confusion was recorded rather than the objective whose teaching covers the content, and C-04 requires cited claims to serve the objective an item practises, so the discriminations are claim-backed where the causes are taught.

deviations.from: the P02 brief, which names parts of 1, 2, 4 and 6 marks for a 14-mark question
deviations.to: five parts: Calculate [1], State [1], Identify [2], Explain [4], Analyse [6]
deviations.why: the named part tariffs sum to 13, so a 1-mark State part was added to reach the stated 14 marks while keeping the named part types and their tariffs intact, as the sibling topics did.

deviations.from: Calculate practice as CALC slots, which the exam exposure for this topic shows three of
deviations.to: Calculate practice carried inside the performance tasks: the data-response part (a) and multiple-choice question 5
deviations.why: the work order is the operative plan and contains no CALC slot; the observed Calculate questions are modelled inside the tasks rather than adding cards beyond the planned count of 20.

deviations.from: OBJ-0455-6.3.2 currency market taught in words and a table only; no card on the sources of supply
deviations.to: ITEM-0455-6.3-017-WHY (sources of supply of a currency) and ITEM-0455-6.3-018-DIAGRAM (a demand and supply diagram for the rand: a rise in export demand shifts demand right and the rand appreciates) added; block 6.3.2-b6 added, a full verbal walk-through of the currency diagram; claims CLM-0455-6.3-021 and 022 added. 018 follows this subject's diagram-card convention: item id suffix DIAGRAM, subtype SYNTH, AO2/AO3, Bloom Apply, Discuss 8, with marking guidance naming every DIAGRAM part plus the SYNTH link and consequence
deviations.why: the syllabus guidance asks for the demand for and supply of a currency and the determination of the equilibrium rate, which is drawn and read as a demand and supply diagram; no diagram was taught or carded; the item schema has no DIAGRAM subtype and this subject renders no charts; the 2026-09 plan showed authors only the objective heading, not the syllabus guidance; fixed 2026-10-13

deviations.from: OBJ-0455-6.3.3 trade cause traced on the export side only
deviations.to: ITEM-0455-6.3-019-CHAIN (a rise in imports raises the supply of the currency and tends to lower the rate) added; block 6.3.3-b7 added and 6.3.3-b2 now names the import side; claim CLM-0455-6.3-023 added
deviations.why: the syllabus guidance names changes in demand for exports and imports; the import side was not taught in this topic and had no card; the 2026-09 plan showed authors only the objective heading, not the syllabus guidance; fixed 2026-10-13

deviations.from: audit lead: maximum and minimum prices in the foreign exchange market
deviations.why: the syllabus places maximum and minimum prices in the foreign exchange market under 2.11.2, not under 6.3.1-6.3.5; it belongs to topic 2.11
